why_this_file_exists: The preregistration is not edited in place. Three deviations from it occurred or were discovered before the arm reached its fixed N=40, and the convention of this project is that a deviation is recorded before the next row is banked, not after the result is known.

deviations.what: The prereg names forge.py sha256 13d52d9c00457553... as the verifier. All 18 banked rows carry forge.py f22eede7de2e37b9..., because the harness_smells.scan() static check (Failure 6) landed in forge.verify() at 12:44 on 2026-08-20, after the prereg was written and before the first row was banked. ruler_noise.py's drift guard aborted the first positive-control round on the mismatch; the driver resumed under the new hash.
deviations.consequence: Both arms were scored under the same verifier on every row, so the contrast is internally valid. The prereg does not name the code that scored it. Remaining rounds will be scored under f22eede7 (the committed forge.py), so that all 40 rows share one fingerprint; the prereg's 13d52d9c entry is superseded by this amendment, not by re-scoring.
deviations.reported_where: manuscript, Method > Verifier Integrity and Results > The Positive Control

deviations.what: The lab machine rebooted without a clean shutdown at 13:32:08 on 2026-08-20 (Windows System log: Kernel-Power 41, EventLog 6008) two minutes after the 18th row was banked at 13:29:54, during round 10 of 40. No row was partially written. Two corrected PCIe errors (WHEA-Logger 17) were logged at 13:32:32, after the reboot. The training window (11:29-12:38) and the evaluation window (12:47-13:30) contain zero TDR (Event 4101), WHEA, Kernel-Power, or NVIDIA-provider events.
deviations.consequence: The adapter is not implicated by the prereg's own distrust rule. The run resumes under ruler_noise.py's idempotent resume logic (rounds 1-9 no-op). Session discipline (rule 1 of poscontrol/START-HERE.md) is broken by a reboot: rows banked after the resume are a second session. They will be tagged by timestamp and the comparison will be reported both pooled and per-session; if the two sessions' null arms differ by more than the measured session-to-session drift (~1 pp), the per-session comparison is primary.

deviations.what: On 2026-08-22, while computing per-task behavioral profiles for all arms in data/ruler_noise.jsonl (an analysis aimed at the three orthogonal retrains, not at this arm), the positive-control arm's n=9 aggregate was computed and seen: 0.6179 vs 0.5039, and 0.6186 vs 0.5986 on the typing-forgiven counterfactual.
deviations.consequence: This is a look, and it is disclosed here rather than omitted. The stopping rule is unchanged: N stays 40 per arm, no early stop, and the decision rule (p<.05 AND >= +5.00 pp on the primary metric) is applied only at N=40. The look cannot change N or the rule, and the number is reported in the manuscript explicitly labelled as an interim, non-decisional figure.

added_secondary_analysis_declared_in_adv.what: Welch t-test on the typing-forgiven counterfactual (aggregate_if_typing_imported, an upper bound) for the positive-control arm vs its null, and the per-task delta profile's correlation with the three retrains' mean profile.
added_secondary_analysis_declared_in_adv.why: The retrains' gain was found on 2026-08-22 to be 51-58% attributable to learned `from typing import` emission (Results > The Typing-Import Decomposition). The positive control's interpretation depends on the same decomposition. Declared here before the arm completes so that it is not a post hoc choice.
